content.title: Coachella 2026 Weekend 2 recap: Justin Bieber, Madonna with Sabrina Carpenter, Karol G and more - Los Angeles Times
content.text: Karol G brings Coachella to an explosive close with J Balvin, Peso Pluma and tour announcement Karol G performs at the Coachella stage on Weekend 1 of the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival. (Christina House/Los Angeles Times) Karol G returned to the Coachella stage to recapture the hearts of a swelling crowd as the queen of Day 3. Once again bringing her jaw-dropping crag-like stage set up filled with lights, gyrating dancers and musicians, the Colombian superstar came out with the heat of a fireball right out of the gate with “Latina Foreva.” Her set got some extra pep from Peso Pluma who joined her on stage for their sultry reggaeton duet “Qlona,” which created an explosion of cheers in the crowd. A few songs later, she brought out Becky G to perform their sizzling smash “Mamiii.” The biggest cameo of the night came when J Balvin surprised the crowd by coming out to perform “Ay Vamos,” “Ginza” and “La Canción.”At the end of her performance, the “Bichota” singer let fans know that she will be launching her next tour in support of her latest album, “Tropicoqueta.” Bright orange text on the festival screens of the main stage flashed the words “Nos Vamos de Tour” (we’re going on tour) during the closing song, “Provenza.” Dates for the tour have not yet been announced. The only ground left for Karol G to break? Her own “I have a big, heavy responsibility on me being the first Latina to headline Coachella,” says Karol G. “It’s a good opportunity to get to more people around the world, and I think it’s my opportunity to get them involved in the place that I come from.” (Bexx Francois / For The Times) Before Karol G headlines Sunday night, revisit our interview with her from December.In February of last year, Karol G boarded a private plane out of Burbank with 16 passengers on board. Just minutes after takeoff, the Colombian singer — one of the biggest global stars in Latin and pop music — saw smoke pouring out of the cabin. The pilots signaled for emergency landing maneuvers; her life flashed before her eyes. Read the full story After sold-out Shrine runs, Subtronics takes dubstep to Coachella’s biggest stage Subtronics (Jason Fenmore) Jesse Kardon has come a long way from his days as a teenager messing around with Ableton in his bedroom. The 33-year-old DJ and producer better known as Subtronics is now an established EDM star. Over the last 15 years, he has built a career that has taken him from playing small clubs in his hometown of Philadelphia to a fall headlining set at the Sphere in Las Vegas and then a landmark run of six sold-out shows at L.A.’s Shrine Auditorium in December.Back in 2022, he performed a surprise set at Coachella’s intimate electronic-focused Do Lab stage, but this year marks his proper Indio, Calif., debut where he is the highest-billed dubstep-rooted artist, playing the massive Sahara Tent on Sunday and April 19. He will also perform two Southland shows between his Coachella sets at the Fox Theater in Pomona on Tuesday and at the GV Surf Club in Palm Springs on April 18. Read the full story How to watch Karol G and BigBang on the Coachella Weekend 2 Sunday livestream Karol G headlines the final day of Coachella 2026, bringing Weekend 2 to a close alongside acts like BigBang, FKA Twigs, Laufey, Kaskade and more. (Christina House / Los Angeles Times) Updated April 17 for Coachella Weekend 2.Karol G headlines the final day of Coachella 2026. The festival’s first Latina headliner brought special guests like Mariah Angeliq, Becky G, Cigarettes After Sex and Wisin for Weekend 1. Who might she surprise fans with on Weekend 2? If you’re watching from home, there’s only one way to find out: the Coachella YouTube livestream. Read the full story Coachella’s anarchic hippos are back, now as bumbling media barons Hippos work at art installation “Network Operations” at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival at the Empire Polo Club in Indio on Sunday, April 12. (Christina House/Los Angeles Times) “All Hippos, the drone is in the control room, give us your all.”Vanessa Bonet of the installation art group Dedo Vabo watched over a mission-control monitor deck, as the buzzing craft climbed into room full of braying hippos in rumpled suits. The beasts were, ostensibly, running a menacing communications conglomerate in a satellite tower looking over the main field of Coachella, but now they were spooked. They scampered around the office looming above the Outdoor stage, while delighted fans on the ground watched them flail behind glass. Read the full story Karol G at Coachella was a global hit. Yet other foreign acts fear touring the U.S. Karol G performs at the Coachella stage on the festival’s opening weekend. (Christina House / Los Angeles Times) On the first Sunday night of Coachella, headliner Karol G told her American fans, and her global audience, to keep fighting.“This is for my Latinos that have been struggling in this country lately,” the Colombian superstar told the tens of thousands watching her in person, and many more on the fest’s livestream. She’d recently criticized ICE in a Playboy interview, but this set was about her fans’ resolve. “We want everyone to feel welcome to our culture, so I want everyone to feel proud of where you come from. Don’t feel fear — feel pride!” she said. Read the full story Our Gen X and Gen Z review the Coachella Ferris wheel Justin Bieber’s do-over Coachella set features Sexyy Red, Billie Eilish, Big Sean, SZA Justin Bieber performs at the Coachella Stage during the 2026 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival at Empire Polo Club on April 11, 2026 in Indio, California. (Kevin Mazur / Getty Images for Coachella) Justin Bieber brought out a largely similar headlining set on Weekend 2 of Coachella—with a few major differences. Over the course of a roughly 90-minute performance, Bieber brought several new guests to the party including Sexyy Red on “Sweet Spot,” and an adorably sweet cameo from Billie Eilish at the end of “One Less Lonely Girl.” The special drop-ins continued with back to back songs with Big Sean (“As Long As You Love Me,” and “No Pressure”).Bieber wrapped up the set bringing out songwriting buddy and fellow Coachella performer Dijon on “Devotion” just as he did last weekend, followed by a surprise cameo from SZA who jumped on stage to a wave of cheers as she and Biebs performed her 2023 hit “Snooze,” with Bieber who ended the night solo on “Daisies” before flooding the sky with fireworks and saying goodnight.Checkout the complete setlist below:“All I Can Take”“Speed Demon”“First Place”“Go Baby”“Butterflies”“Lyin’”“Walkin’ Away”“All the Way”“405”“Too Long”/ “Petting Zoo”/ “I Do”“Sweet Spot” (with Sexyy Red)“Mother in You” (acoustic)“Things You Do” (acoustic)“Glory Voice Memo” (acoustic)“Zuma House” (acoustic)“Dotted Line” (acoustic)“Everything Hallelujah” (acoustic)“One Time““U Smile”“Up”“Baby”“One Less Lonely Girl” (with Billie Eilish)“As Long as You Love Me” (with Big Sean)“No Pressure” (with Big Sean)“Cry Me a River” (Justin Timberlake cover)“Yukon”“Devotion” (with Dijon)“Snooze “(with SZA) The Strokes’ background visuals appear to get cut during the song ‘Oblivius’ As the Strokes’ set came to a close on Coachella’s main stage Saturday night, the band ended with the 2016 song “Obvlius” while a slideshow of various world leaders who were alleged to have been overthrown by the CIA played in the background, including Omar Torrijos, former leader of Panama, Jacobo Árbenz, former president of Guatemala, and Jaime Roldós Aguilera former president of Ecuador. An image of Martin Luther King Jr. was also included, before citing on the screen that “US Govt found guilty of his murder in civil trial.” Video of the set appears to show the screen behind the band going black after images of air missile strikes in Gaza. What we captured at Coachella Ricaviannca Del Mundo of Los Angeles dances during Justin Bieber’s performance at the Coachella stage on Weekend 1 of the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival. (Christina House/Los Angeles Times) See our best photos from Weekend 1. Snoop Dogg pops up during Giveon’s set at Coachella Stage R&B powerhouse Giveon welcomed Snoop Dogg to his main stage Coachella set Saturday evening for a surprise slate of duets that sent crowds sprinting towards the stage amid the last of the afternoon light. With the iconic opening chimes of Dr. Dre’s “Nuthin’ But A ‘G’ Thang,” Long Beach’s prodigal son stepped out and dropped a few bars as Giveon, also a Long Beach native, formalized the Doggfather’s presence with an introduction. The two then dueted to Snoop’s 2003 Pharrell collab “Beautiful,” backed by Giveon’s band. Sombr brings out Billy Idol for ‘Eyes Without a Face’ Sombr has a thing for hitmakers named Billy.For Weekend 1, he brought out Billy Corgan to do Smashing Pumpkins’ “1979.”Tonight, he brought out Billy Idol, who was announced to be in the new class of the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame earlier this week, and guitarist Steve Stevens to do “Eyes Without a Face.” Olivia Rodrigo joins Addison Rae on the Coachella stage Addison Rae brought out a special guest for her Weekend 2 Coachella set: Olivia Rodrigo. Rodrigo performed her new single, “Drop Dead,” which premiered on Friday, during Rae’s set. They also performed a duet on Rae’s “Headphones On,” the Southern California News Group reported. Coachella 2026: Nine Inch Noize revamps industrial rock for a ghoulish rave Nine Inch Noize performs at the Sahara stage during the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival at the Empire Polo Club in Indio on Saturday, April 11, 2026. (Christina House/Los Angeles Times) Last week we caught Nine Inch Noize, the collaboration between Trent Reznor of Nine Inch Nails and Boys Noize. They are back on stage again tonight. Here’s what the Weekend 1 set was like.Trent Reznor might never escape those ghouls. Read the full story Sombr is 2025’s sultry alt-pop star. Can he join the rock greats too? “Yeah, it’s scary,” Shane Boose of Sombr said, about sudden fame. “I thought there was no possibility that I could ever have a hit song. The last thing I want is for people’s opinions, or me being in the public eye, to affect the art I’m creating.” (Evelyn Freja / For The Times) Sombr’s Coachella Weekend 1 set at the Outdoor Theatre was packed and included Billy Corgan as a special guest. Check out our interview with Shane Boose from last year. Back in August, the 20-year-old Shane Boose of Sombr threw his record release party on the patio of the Chateau Marmont in West Hollywood. Sombr’s debut album, “I Barely Know Her,” wouldn’t be out for a few days yet, but under the patio’s twinkling fairy lights, he was already sweating the numbers a bit. Read the full story Kacey Musgraves rides into her surprise set on horseback at Mojave US singer-songwriter Kacey Musgraves performs onstage during the Austin City Limits (ACL) Music Festival at Zilker Park on October 13, 2019 in Austin, Texas. (Suzanne Cordiero/ Getty Images) With the sun perched high over the Indio sky on Saturday, Coachella’s mid-afternoon energy was also plenty warm thanks to the magnetically poetic country of Kacey Musgraves which drew an overflowing crowd to the Mojave tent at 3 p.m. Though she’s a shoo-in favorite for country crowds at Stagecoach, Musgraves, who made her Coachella debuit in 2019, was ready to welcome all comers with her mix of sleek Y2k-era pop, roots music and many shades of sound in between. Her cool and confident cowgirl aura pairs well with a stroll through the wide open polo field, whether on foot—or on a horse. Musgraves opted for the latter as she entered her set on horseback wearing a white tank top, blue jeans and a cream-colored Stetson hat. Backed by a full band and a custom horse trailer on stage, she strummed the chords of aptly-chosen set opener “Middle of Nowhere,” which bled into another new track, “Back on the Wagon” touting a message of standing-by-your-man, followed by “Justified.” Sabrina Carpenter speakeasy? Inside 3 secret Coachella bars Justin Bieber is back at Coachella Saturday night. We ranked his hits Justin Bieber performs last week at the Coachella festival in Indio. (Kevin Mazur / Getty Images for Coachella) In the weeks before Justin Bieber’s headlining performance at this month’s Coachella festival — the 32-year-old teen-pop survivor’s first major concert after a lengthy stretch in the celebrity wilderness — speculation began to mount that he planned to play only songs from his recent “Swag” and “Swag II” albums.And indeed, for 45 minutes or so last Saturday, it seemed like that was what he’d come to do as he sang new song after new song on Coachella’s giant main stage. But then he pulled out a laptop, fired up YouTube and started singing along with some of his old hits — a thrilling subversion of our expectations for a big festival set and a poignant act of self-examination by an artist who’s lived more than half of his life on our screens. (Christina House / Los Angeles Times) Updated April 17 for Coachella Weekend 2.Justin Bieber returns to the Coachella main stage for a headlining performance following his buzzy Weekend 1 show, which featured tracks from both “Swag” albums and his catalog of pop hits from early on in his career. But Weekend 2 isn’t just a greatest hits replay of last weekend. Read the full story Pay $4,000 for your Coachella ticket? This California bill may curb scalping Sophia Peterson, left, and Ariana Pellegrini of Los Angeles dance as DJ Fifi plays at the DoLab during the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival at the Empire Polo Club in Indio on Friday, April 10, 2026. (Christina House / Los Angeles Times) Coachella is never cheap, much less this year’s sold-out edition with the long-awaited live return of Justin Bieber. But if you’re looking to score a last-minute pass, you likely lost your swag when you saw the resale prices on secondary sites like StubHub. As of Friday afternoon, you’ll pay between $4,000 and $5,000 for a sold-out weekend one GA pass on StubHub. (Prices are lower for weekend two on Coachella’s official resale site. Weekend one tickets originally retailed for $649). Here’s what to eat and drink at Coachella Weekend 2 What it’s like to DJ at Coachella: Backstage access, celebrities and lines nobody can avoid Kailyn Brown, who goes by Kailyn Hype, during her DJ set at the Party in My Living Room activation at Coachella. (Kayla Bartkowski / Los Angeles Times) Since I started DJing nearly a decade ago, it’s been a dream of mine to DJ at a music festival, a place where music lovers of all walks of life converge. So when I got the opportunity to spin at Coachella, the country’s festival of all festivals, I was over the moon.This was my second time playing at Coachella with Party in My Living Room, a house party concert series founded by Inglewood native Yannick “Thurz” Koffi in 2015. The activation, designed to look like an actual living room with couches and artwork, was a collaboration with GV Black, a group promoting “Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC) to be seen at the festival.” For the last four years, Koffi has been inviting DJs and musicians (Ty Dolla Sign, P-Lo, Kamaiyah and Isaiah Rashad, to name a few) to perform at the pop-up, which has quickly become a popular side quest for festivalgoers. So when Koffi asked me to be a part of the stacked lineup during Weekend 1, I was honored. Read the full story Anyma finally performs at Coachella, brings out Muse’s Matt Bellamy Nearly 15 minutes after his performance time was scheduled to start, Italian EDM artist Anyma finally took the Coachella stage on Friday of Weekend 2 for the much-anticipated debut of his “Æden” set. (It was canceled Weekend 1 due to the wind.)On the livestream, it appeared that classic Greek and Roman-style columns materialized out of thin air and broke apart repeatedly in a digital trick that made them look like they were floating over the crowd. There were also six large columns actually placed on the festival’s largest stage that framed many of the digital effects and images on the screen.On the livestream, the graphics, which included a statue-like man, a woman made out of lightning and Medusa, looked almost three-dimensional, like they could pluck Anyma from the stage and send him back in time. About 15 minutes into the set, Muse’s Matt Bellamy appeared on stage to sing. (I thought I saw him last week hanging around the Turnstile set!)Lisa from Blackpink was a hotly rumored guest for the set, too. Fans wait for Anyma to perform After Anyma had to cancel the world premiere of “Æden” at Coachella Weekend 1 due to wind, there was a lot of hype for the Italian EDM artist’s performance at Weekend 2.However, concerns started to bubble up once the clock hit midnight, when Anyma was supposed to start playing and the stage was still dark. It looked like the other late-night performers, Sexxy Red in the Sahara Tent and Blood Orange in the Mojava Tent, were also a few minutes behind on the livestream, but they both started by 12:10 a.m. while the main stage feed just continued to show scenes from the festival at night. Madonna and Sabrina Carpenter sing ‘Like a Prayer’ at Coachella Weekend 2 Coachella 2026: Sabrina Carpenter brings out Madonna to perform new song ‘Bring Your Love’ Madonna joined Sabrina Carpenter at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival on Friday night. On stage she reminisced about performing at the festival 20 years ago in the Sahara Tent, shown here. (Spencer Weiner / Los Angeles Times) Anyone who thinks Coachella’s biggest surprises are reserved for Weekend 1 was proved wrong Friday night as Sabrina Carpenter welcomed Madonna on stage during her Weekend 2 headlining set. The crowd exploded with waves of cheers as the iconic pop star came on stage.Madge joined Carpenter as a surprise guest during “Juno,” in which Carpenter reemerged in a gown that was a nod to Botticelli’s “The Birth of Venus” for a torch-passing duet of Madonna’s 1990 pop-house gauntlet “Vogue.” Read the full story See Madonna perform ‘Vogue’ with Sabrina Carpenter Madonna joins Sabrina Carpenter at Coachella, reflects on her first appearance at fest Those extra minutes added to Sabrina Carpenter’s headlining set at Coachella for Weekend 2? It was a special guest and it was Madonna, who came out to sing “Vogue” and an unreleased track with Carpenter.Madonna thanked Carpenter for letting her join the show. “Whatever you want,” Carpenter replied. Madonna talked about performing in the Sahara Tent 20 years ago in 2006.“It was the first time I performed ‘Confessions on the Dance Floor Part I,’” Madonna said.She said she’s wearing the same boots, corset and jacket she wore in 2006. Earlier this week, Madonna announced that she will release “Confessions II” in July. “This is probably the first time I’ve ever performed with someone shorter than me,” Madonna said.Then they sang “Like a Prayer” and a choir joined them before the Queen of Pop exited the stage and Carpenter played “Espresso.” Terry Crews joins the Sabrina Carpenter party and sings Vanessa Carlton Terry Crews replaced Will Ferrell as the stage tech during Sabrina Carpenter’s headlining set during Weekend 2. He also started stripping off his coveralls and sang a bit of Vanessa Carlton’s “A Thousand Miles,” referencing a scene in “White Chicks.”Carlton was actually in the desert last week to perform that song with Teddy Swims, but she wasn’t there Weekend 2. Crews had the crowd singing along while Carpenter had a costume change. Sabrina Carpenter plus Thelma and Louise at Coachella Last week we had a Susan Sarandon monologue in the middle of the Sabrina Carpenter headlining set and this week we have more Hollywood star power with Geena Davis stepping into the role.Davis and Sarandon starred together in 1991 film “Thelma & Louise.”The bit features the actors in a classic car portraying an older version of Carpenter reflecting on her youth, career and fame. Sabrina Carpenter heads back to Sabrinawood for Weekend 2 Sabrina Carpenter is back at Coachella for Weekend 2 and so far her set is lining up with Weekend 1, which is to be expected with the level of production she brought to her headlining set. The opening with Sam Elliott as a cop who pulls her over, the drive-in theater and the catwalk of stars are all back, as is the Sabrinawood set on the main stage.There’s no sign of Susan Sarandon just yet, though. Read more about Sabrina Carpenter’s Weekend 1 set. Waiting for Sabrina Carpenter and maybe a special guest Sabrina Carpenter is expected to take the Coachella stage at 9 p.m. and the rumors are flying that she’s bringing out a special guest since her set is 10 minutes longer than Weekend 1. Will it be Madonna or Taylor Swift, as the internet is guessing? Maybe we’ll get an extra-long Susan Sarandon monologue to fill the time. Here’s how to watch Sabrina Carpenter on the Coachella Weekend 2 livestream. Katseye returns to Coachella. Will it be as ‘Golden’ as last week? Katseye’s Weekend 1 set got a “Golden” surprise a la “KPop Demon Hunters.” Here’s a look before the group returns to the Sahara Tent for Weekend 2. Yuma Tent hits capacity during Kettama Last weekend I remember getting an alert from the Coachella app that Sean Paul’s set at the Heineken House was at capacity on Saturday night, but this is the first such alert for Weekend 2. The app sent a push that Yuma is at capacity with a note directing people to other stages just after 6:30 p.m. Friday.Irish producer/DJ Kettama is the who has packed Yuma this evening, unless everyone wants to get inside to get a glimpse of the shark-shaped disco ball. David Lee Roth joins Teddy Swims again (Christina House/Los Angeles Times) Last weekend, Teddy Swims had one of the most guest-filled sets with Joe Jonas, Vanessa Carlton and David Lee Roth. This week, only Roth showed up. He and Swims performed Van Halen’s “Jump” again and the only real difference was the outfits. Swims swapped Weekend 1’s blue threads for red and Roth swapped his silver and black chevron pants, he deemed a tribute to Artemis II mission, to a pair in white and black.However, over in the Sahara Tent French DJ Hugel brought out French Montana and Ty Dolla $ign. Weekend 1 he brought out Snoop Dogg.ICYMI, we talked to Roth after the performance last week and it’s a doozy of an interview. Who will Teddy Swims bring out this week? Teddy Swims is about to start his set on the main stage in a few minutes. Last week he brought out a Jonas Brother, Vanessa Carlton and David Lee Roth as special guests. The Times caught up with David Lee Roth after the set to find out what he had to say about his first trip to Coachella. How to watch Friday’s Coachella Weekend 2 livestream Bini performs at the Mojave Stage during Weekend 1 of the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival. (Christina House/Los Angeles Times) Coachella Weekend 2 is underway and the YouTube livestream is just getting started. See the full schedule of who’s on today on which channel, including Sabrina Carpenter, Bini, Katseye, Turnstile and the redemption of Anyma, who had to cancel last week’s set due to the winds. Most of the sets are happening concurrently with the stream, but early in the day you will see some prerecorded sets. Remember, the difference for Weekend 2 is that the stream subs in the Yuma Tent for Sonora. More: How to watch Coachella Weekend 2 from home on Friday. Here’s what’s inside the Radiohead bunker at Coachella (Mark Potts / Los Angeles Times) Radiohead isn’t playing Coachella this year — but the English art-rock band is still here.The desert festival has a new space for 2026 called the Bunker, which Radiohead has taken over to premiere an audiovisual installation that looks back at its albums “Kid A” and “Amnesiac” on the occasion of both albums’ turning a quarter-century old. The Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival returns to the Empire Polo Club in Indio, Calif., for its 25th anniversary, with a sold-out crowd for its twin weekends and millions of people watching the livestream from home. Karol G performs at the Coachella stage. Read the full story Meet Slayyyter at her most raw, as the ‘Worst Girl in America’ Pop musician Slayyyter, 29, who is releasing an album at the end of the month titled “Worst Girl in America” and performing at Coachella in April. (Christina House / Los Angeles Times) Slayyyter crawls in through the window of her pseudo-childhood home, her long blond waves damp from a night out and the fringe of her Western jacket swinging as she reaches for a beer in the fridge. Her dad is screaming at her as she escapes to her room; as he bangs on the bedroom door, she reaches for a shotgun.There, surrounded by plush bunny toys, pink lace curtains and a cross on the wall, Slayyyter shoots her dad. And so begins the music video for “Dance…,” the opening track of her new album, “Worst Girl in America.” Read the full story The great Coachella vibe shift Two women pose for a photo last weekend during the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival. The event returns to the Empire Polo Club in Indio this weekend. (Kayla Bartkowski / Los Angeles Times) Commenters who never have been — and never will go — complain about the cost, the influencers, the hype. Purists wax poetic about the days when they disappeared into three days of music and the field wasn’t overtaken by brands like Barbie and e.l.f. cosmetics. Defenders claim they can camp their way to an affordable weekend, and others spend the whole time posting. A select few even talk about great performances they saw — it’s still a music festival. But one thing everybody can agree on: Coachella has changed. I should know. I’ve been covering it as a journalist since 2007.Rapid advancements in technology and mass adoption of social media have brought out the best and worst of the festival — not just on screens thousands of miles away, but to those of us trying not to trip over the makeshift photoshoot you might have seen on Instagram. Read the full story CMAT came to Coachella with politics on her mind and an Irish dance step for California Irish country-pop star CMAT has made her Coachella debut after achieving major fame at home. (Sarah Doyle) Seven months after the release of country-pop star CMAT’s (Ciara Mary-Alice Thompson) third album, Euro-Country, her image appears everywhere across her home country of Ireland. Murals capture her high, flame-red hair and thrifted gowns. Her face appears on tourist shop merchandise and, as she puts it with typical precision, even on preset Redbubble cushion covers. Her writing, like her persona, thrives on noticing the oddly specific ways cultural saturation shows up.It’s a culture she’s always longed to play a starring role in. As a child, she wished for fame every time she blew out her birthday candles. Sitting at the Chateau Marmont two days after her debut Coachella set, it seems that wish has finally come true. Read the full story Coachella is more expensive than ever. Here are 5 great meals for $20 or less (Los Angeles Times photo illustration; photographs by Danielle Dorsey) Coachella Weekend 1 concluded with a historic performance by the festival’s first Latina headliner Karol G and now, attendees are sounding off online about their experiences and offering advice to Weekend 2 festivalgoers. Alongside the mixed reactions to Justin Bieber’s YouTube-fueled set, a key concern has emerged: the three-day festival is now more expensive than ever, including the food.General admission tickets start at $549 for Weekend 1 before taxes, and with shuttle services and on-site camping, can top more than $800. Nearby accommodations are often inflated during April’s festival season and those driving into the fest are also facing a recent surge in gas prices amid the ongoing war in Iran. The Weekend 2 livestream features Anyma, Sabrina Carpenter, Katseye and more. (Christina House/Los Angeles Times) Updated April 16 for Coachella Weekend 2. Sabrina Carpenter is back to headline the first day of Weekend 2 at Coachella 2026 at 9 p.m. Friday. She brought “Sabrinawood” to the desert alongside Susan Sarandon and some classic cars for Weekend 1. It’s worth noting that her set time is 10 minutes longer this weekend. What does she have in store? We’ll be watching Coachella’s YouTube livestream to find out. Read the full story Coachella 2026: We talked to L.A.’s beloved Bob Baker Marionettes about the festival L.A.’s Bob Baker Marionettes performed at the Gobi Stage during the 2026 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival. (Kayla Bartkowski / Los Angeles Times) It’s been a big week for L.A.’s Bob Baker Marionette Theater — it made its Coachella debut and entered an agreement to purchase the Highland Park theater it has been renting since 2019.Last Friday afternoon, hundreds of people packed into Coachella’s red-walled Gobi Tent tent to watch the show. Puppeteers, dressed in the classic Bob Baker red from head to toe, brought out some of the company’s beloved icons — including the show’s host, Pink Cat, adorned in sequins and jewelry. “Puppet-chella … meeeeooowww!” boomed the puppet as she took the stage. (Kayla Bartkowski / Los Angeles Times) The Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival’s encore weekend kicks off at the Empire Polo Club in Indio on Friday with some notable differences from Weekend 1 — beyond the fact that Weekend 2 gets less grass on the fields.Anyma’s world premiere is back on track Read the full story Coachella 2026: Everything you need to know to survive and thrive at the festival — or watch at home The sun sets behind the palm trees at the 2024 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival. (Christina House/Los Angeles Times) It’s almost time to make the annual pilgrimage to the desert for the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival. The event will celebrate its 25th year on the polo fields in Indio, this time with Sabrina Carpenter, Justin Bieber and Karol G topping the lineup. Whether you’re heading to the festival or watching from home, we’ve compiled a guide for maximizing your Coachella time from what to pack and what parties and pop-ups are open to the public to how to watch from the comfort of your couch.
